_comment: Target schema. A target is instance data, so the real ones live outside this repo,
at ~/.agents/work/<project>/showcase/target.json. Scripts take a bare name and
resolve it there, or an explicit path.
Everything here is about what the camera sees and what the copy may claim. Nothing
in a target is a credential.
name: example-app

app._comment: url is where the demo starts. Record against whichever build actually answers: a signed-out production instance that refuses the action makes a useless film. Hide the dev-only chrome instead, below.
app._hostPattern: Regex matched against location.hostname. Zoom, dev-chrome hiding and cursor scaling apply only to hosts that match, so a third-party page in the same take is filmed untouched.
app._viewport: Playwright records at CSS-pixel size and ignores deviceScaleFactor, so record a native 1080p viewport and use zoom for legibility.
app._zoom: CSS zoom on <html>. Never a transform on <html>: that stops fixed-position children painting at all. 1.4 fills a 1080p frame with large type while leaving the app about 1370 CSS px to lay out in.

devChrome._comment: Anything the dev build shows that production does not. Hide it at record time, not in post: anything overlapping a live control cannot be patched without smearing the control.

sources._comment: Third-party material that may appear on camera. Filming inside a competitor's product hands them the frame.

allowed.why: public-domain primary source, not a rival product

copy._comment: Constraints on the post that ships with the video. The lane rules, not the words.

bannedTerms.why: means something else to this audience

rules: No dated claims: a figure true on the recording day expires overnight.
Do not quote on-screen UI labels. They change between runs and the copy silently stops matching.

publish._comment: Where the draft is staged. Never a token: the publishing tool holds its own credentials.
publish._manualSend: Human publication is the default. Staging a draft does not authorize scheduling or publishing.
